# Doris "Dorie" Miller (1919-1943)

## Overview
Doris Miller was an African American U.S. Navy messman who became one of the first American heroes of World War II for his actions during the attack on Pearl Harbor.

## Early Life
- Born October 12, 1919, in Waco, Texas
- Third of four sons to Henrietta and Connery Miller
- Worked as a farmer before enlisting in the Navy in 1939

## Naval Service
- Enlisted as a mess attendant (one of the few roles open to Black sailors at the time)
- Served aboard the USS *West Virginia* (BB-48)
- Was the ship's heavyweight boxing champion

## Pearl Harbor Heroism (December 7, 1941)
During the Japanese attack, Miller:
- Helped move the mortally wounded Captain Mervyn Bennion
- Manned an anti-aircraft machine gun despite having no formal training
- Reportedly shot down enemy aircraft (exact number disputed)
- Continued fighting until ordered to abandon ship

## Recognition
- Awarded the Navy Cross on May 27, 1942 (presented by Admiral Chester Nimitz)
- First African American to receive this honor

## Death
- Killed in action November 24, 1943, when the escort carrier USS *Liscome Bay* was torpedoed near the Gilbert Islands

## Legacy
- USS *Miller* (FF-1091) named in his honor (1973)
- USS *Doris Miller* (CVN-81), a Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, currently under construction
